payload.summary: gm Q&A leak prevention is by WHITELIST CONSTRUCTION, not by instructing the model. src/gm/qa.ts visibleFactsFor() builds an enumerated VisibleFacts bundle and questionMessages() is assembled from that bundle alone. Included: turn number, the asked suspect's token position, the asker's character + position, the player characters still in the running, and COUNTS of suggestions heard / gone unrefuted. Deliberately EXCLUDED, each for a concrete leak reason: (a) the case file; (b) every hand INCLUDING the asker's own — a suspect has no business knowing who holds what, and passing it would put six card names in a prompt for no gain; (c) the event log — suggestion-made events name arbitrary cards, so the log is the single easiest way to leak the answer (a suggester who names the true triple and goes unrefuted has all three answers sitting in their own visible log); (d) weapon positions and non-player suspect token positions — same leak, less obvious. tests/gm/qa.test.ts asserts on the CAPTURED REQUEST BODY of the real in-process vendor, in a game whose visible log genuinely contains all three case-file card names, that none of the 21 cards appears outside the stated whitelist. WHOEVER BUILDS THE CLI MUST NOT WIDEN THIS BUNDLE: passing a playerView straight through to a prompt re-opens the leak.

PlayerView gap found while building the opponent policy, load-bearing for the CLI item and for anyone extending the AI seats. The engine's PlayerView does NOT expose Player.movedBySuggestion or Player.hasSuggestedThisTurn. hasSuggestedThisTurn IS reliably derivable from the event log (scan back to the last turn-started naming this seat, then look for a suggestion-made by this seat after it) and src/gm/opponent.ts does exactly that — it is what stops the policy suggesting twice in one turn. movedBySuggestion is NOT reliably derivable, so the policy FORGOES a real Clue rule: a seat dragged into a room by someone else's suggestion may suggest from there at the start of its next turn without moving (canSuggest() returns true in awaiting-roll for exactly that case), and the policy just rolls instead. This costs the AI seats a free suggestion now and then; it never makes an illegal move. The fix, if it is wanted, is an engine change (add movedBySuggestion to PlayerView), which is out of scope for item k0n64xb4 and belongs to the engine slice.

Token-ledger semantics worth a panel eye (resolution 5rwbt08h, token-count attribution v1). ChatClient#account runs only after a SUCCESSFUL parse, so SessionUsage.calls counts COMPLETED responses; a call that 4xx/5xx/timed out is invisible in the ledger. Consequence, pinned by a test in tests/gm/game-master.test.ts: a session in which every LLM call failed reports usage.calls === 0, and src/gm/index.ts formatUsageLedger() then prints 'No LLM calls were made this session.' — literally true of accounted calls, misleading about what the session attempted. I did not change the llm slice for this (it is a sibling item, in review). Options for the closer: leave it and document, or have ChatClient count attempts separately from accounted calls. formatUsageLedger already names callsWithoutUsage ('N calls reported no usage and are not counted above') so providers that omit usage are honest; it is only the FAILED calls that vanish.

The corrected refutation rule now ships in src/gm/notebook.ts and the engine playthrough test DELEGATES to it instead of carrying its own copy (no-duplication rule). buildNotebook(playerView) implements: a named card proven in ANOTHER player's hand is excluded from what the refuter could have shown; a named card proven to be the REFUTER'S OWN stays a candidate; a card proven to be in the case file is excluded; a lone survivor is proven held by the refuter; iterate to fixpoint. It adds one inference the engine bot only had as an ad-hoc branch: MY OWN unrefuted suggestion proves every named card not in my hand is in the case file (nobody but the suggester could hold them). That ad-hoc branch in tests/engine/playthrough.test.ts was deleted as dead code. tests/gm/notebook.test.ts pins the exact shape that breaks the naive rule — p1 knows Mrs. White is p3's and the Dagger is p2's, p2 then suggests Mrs. White + Dagger in the Library and p3 refutes; the naive form writes Library -> p3, which is FALSE (p2 holds the Library) — and cross-checks every belief against the dealt truth.

Build complete for item k0n64xb4. src/gm/: notebook.ts (corrected deduction), opponent.ts (deterministic policy: plan from PlayerView, apply through real engine actions), scenario.ts, narrator.ts, qa.ts, index.ts (GameMaster over ONE ChatClient + formatUsageLedger). tests/gm/: notebook, opponent, scenario, narrator, qa, game-master + support.ts. Whole repo 265 pass / 0 fail across 15 files (was 215 before this slice), bunx tsc --noEmit clean under the strict tsconfig. No mocks anywhere: the LLM tests drive the real in-process fake vendor over TCP, the engine tests drive real actions. Evidence the policy is a real player, not a stub: all-AI games at 3, 4, 5 and 6 seats each terminate with exactly ONE accusation and it is always correct — the policy accuses only when the notebook leaves exactly one candidate triple, so it never accuses wrongly in a whole game. LIVE smoke against the real endpoint (https://api.poe.com/v1, claude-sonnet-4.5): requestScenario returned source='llm' in ONE call — Poe honours response_format json_object, no retry needed — and the ledger reported 1391 tokens (908 prompt + 483 completion) read from the response's own usage object.

bindings.change-summary:
GAME MASTER (item k0n64xb4) — CHANGE SUMMARY

src/gm/ in six modules, on branch epic/murder-mystery-game, 4 commits.
  notebook.ts  closed-world deduction over a PlayerView, implementing the CORRECTED refutation
               rule from the engine finding (run e6g6g38j): a named card proven in ANOTHER
               player's hand is excluded, a card proven to be the REFUTER'S OWN stays a
               candidate, fixpoint until nothing new. Plus: my own unrefuted suggestion proves
               every named card I do not hold is in the case file.
  opponent.ts  deterministic policy — plan from a PlayerView, apply through the REAL engine
               action. Settles owed refutations, accuses only when the notebook leaves exactly
               one triple, else walks toward the nearest unvisited candidate room via
               legalDestinations and suggests the least-tested suspect/weapon still open.
  scenario.ts  one setup call (json_object) for victim/setting/intro/six personas; parses
               defensively and degrades FIELD BY FIELD to a canned, card-free scenario. A
               provider that rejects response_format is retried once without it.
  narrator.ts  one batched call per turn, prompted with the engine's own describeEvent
               sentences; any failure or bad entry falls back to that sentence VERBATIM.
  qa.ts        in-fiction Q&A whose prompt is built from an enumerated whitelist of visible
               facts — never the case file, never any hand (including the asker's), never the
               event log, never the weapon board.
  index.ts     GameMaster over ONE shared ChatClient with per-role model overrides, plus
               formatUsageLedger() for per-model token totals (resolution 5rwbt08h).

Tests: tests/gm/ (6 files + support.ts), no mocks — the real in-process fake vendor over TCP for
every LLM path, real engine actions for every game path. Whole repo 265 pass / 0 fail across 15
files (215 before), `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

Load-bearing evidence: all-AI games at 3/4/5/6 seats each end with exactly ONE accusation and it
is always correct; the Q&A test asserts on the CAPTURED REQUEST BODY, in a game whose visible log
names all three case-file cards, that no card outside the whitelist reaches the vendor; a live
smoke against api.poe.com (claude-sonnet-4.5) returned source='llm' in one call, 1391 tokens read
from the response's own usage object.

Known gaps journaled, not fixed: PlayerView does not expose movedBySuggestion, so AI seats forgo
the free suggestion when dragged into a room (an engine-view change, out of scope here); and
SessionUsage.calls counts only COMPLETED responses, so an all-failure session reports zero calls.
The engine playthrough test now delegates to notebook.ts and its duplicate algorithm was deleted.

bindings.crit-codex:
codex
`GameMaster.narrate` accepts unfiltered events, so passing raw turn events can send private `refutation-card-shown` identities to the vendor and expose them publicly.
Q&A’s whitelist is bypassed because arbitrary LLM-generated scenario fields—created with every card name in context—are injected into its prompt, while the leakage test covers only the card-free canned scenario.
bindings.crit-agy:
The deduction algorithm in `notebook.ts` contains a fatal logic error by retaining a refuter's shown card as a candidate, preventing the AI from eliminating known cards and forcing it to rely on blindly guessing the solution by pure chance. 
By explicitly excluding the event log and all player hands from the prompt in `qa.ts`, the system deprives the LLM of essential context, rendering the persona completely oblivious to the game's history and its own in-game knowledge during Q&A.

Panel finding [codex] 'GameMaster.narrate accepts unfiltered events' — FIXED, commit e18b68b. Fix: narration is now always FOR someone. NarrationRequest gained a required 'viewer: PlayerId', and narrateEvents filters every candidate event through the engine's own visibility rule before a prompt is built. That rule was extracted from visibleEvents as isVisibleTo(event, playerId) in src/engine/view.ts so loose events are judged by exactly the same predicate the log projection uses — no second implementation to drift. GameMaster.narrate(view, events) takes the PlayerView (symmetry with ask) and derives viewer=view.you, so a caller handing over the raw state.events log can no longer put another player's private refutation-card-shown payload into a vendor request. Events the viewer may not see are DROPPED, not muted — no line, because there is nothing to tell them. An all-invisible batch spends no call. Tests: tests/gm/narrator.test.ts 'the narrator filters for its viewer' drives a real exchange (p2 suggests Reverend Green/Dagger in the Kitchen, p3 holds exactly one match and shows it to p2 alone), hands narrateEvents the RAW tail [suggestion-refuted, refutation-card-shown] as viewer p1, and asserts the captured vendor request body contains no 'Reverend Green' while the viewer-visible 'refutes ... with a card shown in private' fallback line still narrates; companion tests assert p2 (who was shown the card) still gets that line, and that a batch with nothing visible makes no call at all. tests/gm/game-master.test.ts adds the same property at the GameMaster surface with the whole raw log passed in.

Panel finding [agy] 'Q&A persona is history-blind' — FIXED, commit ba58f7b. Fix: VisibleFacts gained recentHistory — the asker's own visible log rendered with the engine's own describeEvent, most recent last, clamped to HISTORY_LIMIT=20 lines, rendered into the user message under 'What the house has seen so far, in order:'. Leak-safety is kept by an explicit ALLOW-LIST (CARD_FREE_HISTORY) of event types whose sentence names no card a PLAYER CHOSE: game-started, turn-started, rolled, moved, secret-passage, suggestion-refuted, suggestion-unrefuted, player-eliminated, turn-ended. Held back: suggestion-made and the token-relocated events it causes (three arbitrary cards), refutation-card-shown (somebody's hand), accusation-made and game-over (the case file). Rationale recorded in the module header: the raw agy proposal was to paste visibleEvents(state, asker) verbatim on the grounds that the asker already knows it, but a suggester who names the true triple and goes unrefuted has all three answers sitting in their own visible log — pasting that would put the case file in a vendor prompt and would have broken the existing whitelist assertions. Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a new event type is withheld until someone decides it is safe. Every listed type is public in the engine (only refutation-card-shown is addressed to particular players), which is what makes the prompt's 'what the house has seen' framing true. Tests in tests/gm/qa.test.ts: captured request quotes the game-started / turn-started / suggestion-unrefuted lines and never the suggestion-made or token-relocated lines; a p2-suggests/p3-refutes exchange puts 'p3 refutes p2's suggestion with a card shown in private.' in the body while Reverend Green, Dagger and Kitchen stay out; visibleFactsFor unit tests pin the exact line set and the 20-line clamp. Existing whitelist assertions unchanged and green.

Panel finding [codex] 'scenario fields could embed the case file' — PREMISE INVALID, hardening tests added instead, commit aacaefd. No production change: scenarioMessages() takes no arguments and requestScenario() takes no GameState, so there is no state available to embed. Two hardening tests pin the boundary. INBOUND (tests/gm/qa.test.ts, 'a hostile LLM-written scenario cannot smuggle state into the facts'): a fake vendor answers the scenario call with card names in the victim, the setting and every persona ('Professor Plum, found in the Study beside the Wrench'; personas naming the Billiard Room and the Revolver), then GameMaster.ask runs the Q&A path on that parsed scenario. Asserts the hostile fiction genuinely reached the model (the persona and setting are in the system message, so the test cannot pass by the scenario being dropped), that the USER message — the facts section, where game state would land — names no card outside the whitelist and specifically none of Professor Plum / Wrench / Study, and that every card in the system message is accounted for by a scenario string: strip victim + setting + the asked persona and the remainder is inside the whitelist again. OUTBOUND (tests/gm/scenario.test.ts, 'the scenario request carries no game state'): the literal check the finding asked for — that the request contains no case-file card and no hand contents — is impossible and would have been a false pass, because the prompt must enumerate the deck for the model to invent fiction about it. Asserted instead: (1) two real arrangedGame() deals with different case files and disjoint hands produce BYTE-IDENTICAL request bodies; (2) each of the 21 cards occurs exactly once in the prompt, so the case-file triple is named neither more nor less than any other card and nothing is singled out; (3) no seat id (p1/p2/p3), no six-card hand run, and no case-file/hand/solution wording appears in the body. Also refactored: messagesOf/messageOfRole added to tests/gm/support.ts (promptTextOf now builds on messagesOf), and one leakedCards() whitelist scan replaces the per-test restatement.

payload.guidance:
Weigh the panel critiques (codex
`GameMaster.narrate` accepts unfiltered events, so passing raw turn events can send private `refutation-card-shown` identities to the vendor and expose them publicly.
Q&A’s whitelist is bypassed because arbitrary LLM-generated scenario fields—created with every card name in context—are injected into its prompt, while the leakage test covers only the card-free canned scenario.
 / The deduction algorithm in `notebook.ts` contains a fatal logic error by retaining a refuter's shown card as a candidate, preventing the AI from eliminating known cards and forcing it to rely on blindly guessing the solution by pure chance. 
By explicitly excluding the event log and all player hands from the prompt in `qa.ts`, the system deprives the LLM of essential context, rendering the persona completely oblivious to the game's history and its own in-game knowledge during Q&A.
) against the code as committed, apply the accepted fixes, journal dispositions, and close the item to in-review.
